docs.title: epc_domestic: column provenance
docs.text:
Where every column of the table epc_domestic comes from, what was done to it, how it is checked and why. Generated from the metadata of uprn-epc version 0.2.0 at commit fa55af5.

The table holds every certificate of the Scottish Government's extended historic extract of domestic Energy Performance Certificates, release 2026Q2, one row per certificate, values exactly as published, with typed copies for joining a cohort by UPRN and date. The table itself is private; this site holds no value of any row, no address and no postcode.

  • Columns: 130 pages, one per column.
  • Pinned sources: the 23 files the build reads or hashes.
  • Decisions: the 12 decisions, in force and history.
  • Checks: what every check family tests and how far it reaches.

The data dictionary, the loader, the join queries and the build record are in the repository. The source archive is held in a restricted Zenodo record whose metadata is public and whose files are on request.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Every check the build can emit, by family (epc_ingest/check_catalogue.yaml). Each is blocking: a failure stops the build and nothing is promoted. A build's manifest records which were emitted and their results; this page defines them and says how far each reaches.

docs.title: source.member
docs.text:
Name pattern ^source\.[^/]+/extracted/\d{4}\.csv$. The annual file's SHA256 equals the pin in sources.yaml, so the bytes read are the bytes reviewed.

Applies to every column. Coverage: every byte of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: source.datazone_list
docs.text:
Name pattern ^source\.datazones/. The data zone reference list's SHA256 equals the pin, the same hash the sibling project pins.

Applies to datazone_2001, datazone_2001_status, datazone_2011, datazone_2011_status. Coverage: every byte of the list. Runs in every build.

docs.title: source.archive
docs.text:
Name pattern ^source\.[^/]+/[^/]+\.7z$. The downloaded archive's SHA256 equals the pin; the build never reads the archive, only the extracted members.

Applies to every column. Coverage: every byte of the archive. Runs only under --verify-archive.

docs.title: source.note
docs.text:
Name pattern ^source\.[^/]+/publication_note\.pdf$. The publication note's SHA256 equals the pin; the note is documentation, the source of the column descriptions.

Applies to no column: table-level. Coverage: every byte of the note. Runs only under --verify-archive.

docs.title: schema.matches_generator
docs.text:
Name pattern ^schema\.matches_generator$. Output_schema.yaml is exactly what python -m epc_ingest.columns writes from published_columns.yaml and the derived list.

Applies to every column. Coverage: every field of the schema. Runs in every build.

docs.title: datazones.count
docs.text:
Name pattern ^datazones_\d{4}\.count$. The reference list holds the pinned number of zones.

Applies to datazone_2001, datazone_2001_status, datazone_2011, datazone_2011_status. Coverage: the whole list. Runs in every build.

docs.title: datazones.distinct
docs.text:
Name pattern ^datazones_\d{4}\.distinct$. No zone code repeats in the reference list.

Applies to datazone_2001, datazone_2001_status, datazone_2011, datazone_2011_status. Coverage: the whole list. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.utf8
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.utf8$. The annual file decodes as UTF-8 with no error.

Applies to every published column. Coverage: every byte of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.header_names
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.header_names$. The first header row equals the 107 pinned machine names, in order.

Applies to every published column. Coverage: the header row. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.header_labels
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.header_labels$. The second header row equals the 107 pinned labels, in order.

Applies to every published column. Coverage: the header row. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.row_width
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.row_width$. Every data row has 107 fields.

Applies to every published column. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.rows
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.rows$. The number of data rows equals the pin for the member, so source_row runs 1 to that number.

Applies to source_year, source_row. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.rrn_shape
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.rrn_shape$. Every non-empty REPORT_REFERENCE_NUMBER has the shape 9999-9999-9999-9999-9999.

Applies to rrn. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.rrn_unique_in_file
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.rrn_unique_in_file$. No non-empty REPORT_REFERENCE_NUMBER repeats within the file.

Applies to rrn. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.created_at_year
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.created_at_year$. Every CREATED_AT falls in the file's year, the rule that places a row in its annual file.

Applies to source_year, created_at_parsed. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.derived_values_parse
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.derived_values_parse$. Every date, timestamp, flag, integer and decimal a derived column needs parses by its rule; one failure stops the build.

Applies to uprn_sepcr, uprn_osg, inspection_date_parsed, lodgement_date_parsed, created_at_parsed, historic_flag, current_energy_efficiency_int, potential_energy_efficiency_int, environment_impact_current_int, environment_impact_potential_int, total_floor_area_int, energy_consumption_current_num, co2_emissions_current_num, co2_emiss_curr_per_floor_area_num. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.text_within_width
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.text_within_width$. No text value is longer than its column's declared nvarchar width.

Applies to every string column. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: year.decimal_round_trip
docs.text:
Name pattern ^\d{4}\.decimal_round_trip$. Every decimal cell survives file text to Decimal to 4-place text to Decimal unchanged, so the CSV, the digest and SQL Server agree to the byte.

Applies to energy_consumption_current_num, co2_emissions_current_num, co2_emiss_curr_per_floor_area_num. Coverage: every row of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: table.rows
docs.text:
Name pattern ^table\.rows$. The key (epc_release, source_year, source_row) is unique over the whole table.

Applies to every key column. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: table.rrn_unique
docs.text:
Name pattern ^table\.rrn_unique$. No rrn repeats across the whole table.

Applies to rrn. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: table.uprn_one_to_one
docs.text:
Name pattern ^table\.uprn_one_to_one$. Each uprn_osg maps to one uprn_sepcr and each uprn_sepcr to one uprn_osg, where both exist.

Applies to uprn_osg, uprn_sepcr. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: table.no_unknown_code
docs.text:
Name pattern ^table\.datazone_\d{4}_status\.no_unknown_code$. No well-formed data zone code is absent from the vintage's reference list.

Applies to datazone_2001, datazone_2001_status, datazone_2011, datazone_2011_status. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: table.required_nonnull
docs.text:
Name pattern ^table\.required_nonnull$. Every column the schema declares NOT NULL has no NULL.

Applies to every nonnull column. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.rows
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.(rows|row_groups)$. The saved Parquet has the rows the CSV has and one row group per annual file.

Applies to every column. Coverage: the whole file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.digest
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.\d{4}\.digest$. The row digest recomputed from the saved Parquet, rendered as the CSV renders it, equals the digest computed while writing the CSV, year by year.

Applies to every exported column. Coverage: every cell of every row. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.one_year_per_row_group
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.\d{4}\.one_year_per_row_group$. Each row group holds one source_year.

Applies to source_year. Coverage: every row of the table. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.structure
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.(column_names|column_types|nullability)$. The saved Parquet's columns, Arrow types and nullability are the schema's.

Applies to every column. Coverage: the schema of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.metadata
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.metadata\.. The saved Parquet carries the build's grain, key, schema version, release, source pins and the hashes of the registry and the decision log.

Applies to no column: table-level. Coverage: the file's metadata. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.parquet.sampled_rows_equal_source
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.parquet\.sampled_rows_equal_source$. For the first, middle and last row of every annual file, every published cell read back from the Parquet equals the raw text of the source file.

Applies to every published column. Coverage: three rows per annual file (SAMPLE_ROWS), not every row; every row is covered by the digest. Runs in every build.

docs.title: readback.csv
docs.text:
Name pattern ^readback\.csv\.(header|rows|digest_total)$. The written CSV read back has the exported header, the row count and the digest total the build recorded.

Applies to every exported column. Coverage: every cell of every row. Runs in every build.

docs.title: Derived columns
docs.text: Column Type Nullable Description rrn text yes The report reference number as published where not empty, NULL where empty (9% of rows, mostly 2013 to 2016). Unique where present. uprn_sepcr 64-bit integer no The register's own 10-digit property reference, trimmed and as an integer. Not the Gazetteer UPRN. Present in every row. uprn_osg 64-bit integer yes The One Scotland Gazetteer UPRN as an integer, NULL where the published cell is empty (4.7% of rows). The only column a join compares; a padded cohort UPRN matches once cast to bigint. pc_norm text yes POSTCODE upper-cased with every space removed, postcode-simd's pc_norm. NULL where the published cell is empty. Nothing repaired. datazone_2001 text yes The 2001 data zone code when DATA_ZONE starts with S01 and six digits followed by a space or the end, otherwise NULL. datazone_2001_status text no code, empty, not_a_datazone (for 00Q, NA and the like) or unknown_code (well formed, not in the pinned list; the build fails if any). datazone_2011 text yes The 2011 data zone code by the same rule, otherwise NULL. datazone_2011_status text no As datazone_2001_status, for the 2011 column. inspection_date_parsed date no INSPECTION_DATE (yyyy-mm-dd) as a date: the day the assessor saw the dwelling. The dated joins choose the certificate by it. A value that does not parse stops the build. lodgement_date_parsed date no LODGEMENT_DATE (yyyy-mm-dd) as a date. The administrative date of the certificate, the same day as the inspection or soon after (median 1 day); the ten-year validity runs from it. Outliers (2002, 2006, 2108) are kept as published. created_at_parsed timestamp no CREATED_AT (dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss) as a timestamp to the second. Its year is the file year. historic_flag flag no 1 where HISTORIC is True (the certificate has been superseded), 0 where False. Any other value stops the build. current_energy_efficiency_int 32-bit integer no The current energy efficiency rating as an integer. A SAP rating runs 1 to 100; values above 100 are publisher errors kept as published and counted in the build report. potential_energy_efficiency_int 32-bit integer no The potential energy efficiency rating as an integer. environment_impact_current_int 32-bit integer no The current environmental impact rating as an integer. environment_impact_potential_int 32-bit integer no The potential environmental impact rating as an integer. total_floor_area_int 32-bit integer no Total floor area in square metres as an integer. 0 in every 2008 and 2009 row. energy_consumption_current_num decimal(19,4) no Primary energy indicator (kWh per square metre per year) as decimal(19,4). co2_emissions_current_num decimal(19,4) no Current emissions (tonnes of CO2 per year) as decimal(19,4). co2_emiss_curr_per_floor_area_num decimal(19,4) no Current emissions per floor area (kg of CO2 per square metre per year) as decimal(19,4).

docs.title: 3_YR_ENERGY_COST_CURRENT
docs.text:
As published. Publisher's label: Total current energy costs over 3 years (�).

Publication note (page 8 under the label Total current energy costs over 3 years; quoted from the Scottish Government's note, SHA256 c2f336967e5d…, Open Government Licence v3.0): Calculation illustrating the total energy cost for heating, cooling, lighting, and ventilating the building. Based on standardised occupancy patterns and fuel costs. (Units: £) Marked in the note as a Scotland-only field.

Group Type Nullable In the CSV SQL Server type published text no yes nvarchar(32) NOT NULL

docs.title: Where it comes from
docs.text:
Field 13 of 107 in every annual file of release 2026Q2, machine name 3_YR_ENERGY_COST_CURRENT, publisher's label "Total current energy costs over 3 years (�)". The row keeps its file position as source_row. The label is as printed in the file's second header row, where the publisher's export already holds the replacement character U+FFFD (shown as �) in place of a lost ² or £; the publication note prints the intended character.

docs.text: copied. the cell's text exactly as published, trailing spaces and embedded newlines included; the empty string where the cell is empty (code: epc_ingest/reader.py: read_year)

docs.title: How it is checked
docs.text:
What each check tests. Whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"], not here.

  • source.member: the annual file's SHA256 equals the pin in sources.yaml, so the bytes read are the bytes reviewed. Coverage: every byte of the file.
  • source.archive: the downloaded archive's SHA256 equals the pin; the build never reads the archive, only the extracted members. Coverage: every byte of the archive. Runs only under --verify-archive.
  • schema.matches_generator: output_schema.yaml is exactly what python -m epc_ingest.columns writes from published_columns.yaml and the derived list. Coverage: every field of the schema.
  • year.utf8: the annual file decodes as UTF-8 with no error. Coverage: every byte of the file.
  • year.header_names: the first header row equals the 107 pinned machine names, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.header_labels: the second header row equals the 107 pinned labels, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.row_width: every data row has 107 fields. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • year.text_within_width: no text value is longer than its column's declared nvarchar width. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • table.required_nonnull: every column the schema declares NOT NULL has no NULL. Coverage: every row of the table.
  • readback.parquet.rows: the saved Parquet has the rows the CSV has and one row group per annual file. Coverage: the whole file.

  • schema.matches_generator: output_schema.yaml is exactly what python -m epc_ingest.columns writes from published_columns.yaml and the derived list. Coverage: every field of the schema.
  • year.utf8: the annual file decodes as UTF-8 with no error. Coverage: every byte of the file.
  • year.header_names: the first header row equals the 107 pinned machine names, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.header_labels: the second header row equals the 107 pinned labels, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.row_width: every data row has 107 fields. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • year.text_within_width: no text value is longer than its column's declared nvarchar width. Coverage: every row of the file.

  • readback.parquet.rows: the saved Parquet has the rows the CSV has and one row group per annual file. Coverage: the whole file.
  • readback.parquet.digest: the row digest recomputed from the saved Parquet, rendered as the CSV renders it, equals the digest computed while writing the CSV, year by year. Coverage: every cell of every row.

docs.title: How it is checked
docs.text:
What each check tests. Whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"], not here.

  • source.member: the annual file's SHA256 equals the pin in sources.yaml, so the bytes read are the bytes reviewed. Coverage: every byte of the file.
  • source.archive: the downloaded archive's SHA256 equals the pin; the build never reads the archive, only the extracted members. Coverage: every byte of the archive. Runs only under --verify-archive.

  • year.header_names: the first header row equals the 107 pinned machine names, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.header_labels: the second header row equals the 107 pinned labels, in order. Coverage: the header row.
  • year.row_width: every data row has 107 fields. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • year.text_within_width: no text value is longer than its column's declared nvarchar width. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • table.required_nonnull: every column the schema declares NOT NULL has no NULL. Coverage: every row of the table.
  • readback.parquet.rows: the saved Parquet has the rows the CSV has and one row group per annual file. Coverage: the whole file.
  • readback.parquet.digest: the row digest recomputed from the saved Parquet, rendered as the CSV renders it, equals the digest computed while writing the CSV, year by year. Coverage: every cell of every row.

What each check tests. Whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"], not here.

  • source.member: the annual file's SHA256 equals the pin in sources.yaml, so the bytes read are the bytes reviewed. Coverage: every byte of the file.
  • source.archive: the downloaded archive's SHA256 equals the pin; the build never reads the archive, only the extracted members. Coverage: every byte of the archive. Runs only under --verify-archive.
  • schema.matches_generator: output_schema.yaml is exactly what python -m epc_ingest.columns writes from published_columns.yaml and the derived list. Coverage: every field of the schema.
  • year.rows: the number of data rows equals the pin for the member, so source_row runs 1 to that number. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • year.created_at_year: every CREATED_AT falls in the file's year, the rule that places a row in its annual file. Coverage: every row of the file.
  • table.rows: the key (epc_release, source_year, source_row) is unique over the whole table. Coverage: every row of the table.
  • table.required_nonnull: every column the schema declares NOT NULL has no NULL. Coverage: every row of the table.
  • readback.parquet.rows: the saved Parquet has the rows the CSV has and one row group per annual file. Coverage: the whole file.
  • readback.parquet.digest: the row digest recomputed from the saved Parquet, rendered as the CSV renders it, equals the digest computed while writing the CSV, year by year. Coverage: every cell of every row.

  • readback.csv: the written CSV read back has the exported header, the row count and the digest total the build recorded. Coverage: every cell of every row.

docs.title: address-lines-loaded
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. Revises recipe-public-data-private on one point. The CSV and the SQL table carry ADDRESS1, ADDRESS2 and ADDRESS3 as published, like every other column. The CSV goes only to the HIC OneDrive and into the HIC SQL Server; nothing built leaves the safe haven. The build report and the data dictionary still print no address or postcode value. A view without the three columns is the suggested analyst-facing object; the question of who may see them stays with information governance.

Why. The address lines are the only key for the 178,537 certificates without a Gazetteer UPRN and the only way to check a UPRN linkage against the cohort's own address; the register is published openly with them, so the table holds nothing the public cannot see, and withholding them protected a file that never leaves HIC.

Amends recipe-public-data-private. Still stands: The built Parquet, CSV and SQL table stay private; the source archive stays in the restricted Zenodo draft; only the withholding of the three address lines from the CSV is changed.

docs.title: bounded-widths-max-in-digest
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. Every text column is nvarchar(n) from the measured longest value with headroom; there is no nvarchar(max). The row digest still converts the first operand of each concatenation chunk to nvarchar(max).

Why. The longest value is 3,330 characters, so widths bound every cell, but CONCAT_WS returns nvarchar(4000) unless an operand is max and a row of bounded cells can exceed that.

docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. The generated BULK INSERT names CODEPAGE = '65001'. The staging columns keep the UTF-8 collation, which governs how the bytes are stored, not how the file is read.

Why. The first container probe loaded 3,787,069 rows and failed the digest on every year; the only cells that differed were those with a non-breaking space, read in the OEM code page as two other characters.

docs.title: derived-names-and-nullability
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. Derived columns carry a kind suffix (_parsed, _flag, _int, _num) or are a new word, never a published name in another case. Published columns are NOT NULL and hold the empty string where the file is empty. Derived columns take the nullability the schema declares; the nullable ones are NULL only in their documented missing case, and a required value that does not parse stops the build.

Why. SQL Server compares identifiers under the database collation, case-insensitive by default. Empty and NULL mean different things and must survive the CSV, the import and the digest (reviews of 30 October 2026).

docs.title: file-year-is-created-at
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-29. Status: in_force.

Decision. The annual file a row belongs to is the year of CREATED_AT, not of LODGEMENT_DATE; the build fails if a row's CREATED_AT year is not the file year.

Why. Measured over every file: CREATED_AT is always in the file year, LODGEMENT_DATE is not (outliers 2002, 2006, 2108).

docs.title: join-by-inspection-date
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. The dated joins choose the certificate by inspection_date_parsed, the latest on or before the cohort date, and return both the inspection and the lodgement date, the age in days from the inspection, and a flag for a lodgement before its inspection. The two join indexes key on inspection_date_parsed.

Why. The inspection is when the assessor saw the dwelling; lodgement is the administrative date that follows it (same day in 1,622,516 certificates, 1 to 7 days in 1,513,733, 8 to 30 in 378,567, 31 to 365 in 244,711, over a year in 25,506, before the inspection in 2,036). For an exposure as of a date the inspection is the right anchor; validity still runs from lodgement.

Amends join-latest-lodged-with-ties. Still stands: The tie rule (two or more certificates on the latest eligible day are ambiguous_as_of), the undated latest-certificate rule and its statuses, and that the query never decides expiry; only the date the dated joins rank by is changed, from lodgement to inspection.

docs.title: join-latest-lodged-with-ties
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. The example join returns the latest certificate lodged on or before the cohort date, with its age in days, and does not decide expiry. Two or more certificates of one UPRN lodged on the latest eligible day are ambiguous_as_of with no values. Without a date, the HISTORIC = False certificate; two of them are ambiguous_latest; none is no_current_certificate.

Why. The choice of certificate must be explicit in the query, never a default or an arbitrary TOP (1).

Amended by join-by-inspection-date.

docs.title: one-table-per-certificate
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-29. Status: in_force.

Decision. One table, epc_domestic, one row per published certificate, superseded certificates included, keyed by (epc_release, source_year, source_row).

Why. The published grain is the certificate. REPORT_REFERENCE_NUMBER is empty in 9% of rows and (BUILDING_REFERENCE_NUMBER, CREATED_AT) repeats, so no published key exists; the file position is the only stable identity. A later quarterly release is a new build with a new epc_release, never an update.

docs.title: recipe-public-data-private
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. The repository publishes the recipe and cites the source. The built Parquet, CSV and SQL table stay private; the three address lines are withheld from the CSV; the source archive is held as an unpublished restricted Zenodo draft (23784712) as the off-site copy.

Why. The address and postcode fields are under a Royal Mail notice, not the Open Government Licence, and the download URL is overwritten every quarter.

Amended by address-lines-loaded.

docs.title: uprn-as-integer
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-30. Status: in_force.

Decision. uprn_osg is a bigint and is the only column any join compares. The published text stays as provenance. Short UPRNs are real, not truncated.

Why. Every one of the 17,933 8-digit UPRNs exists in OS Open UPRN and lies in Clackmannanshire; length follows the issuing council (docs/uprn_check_2026-10-30.md). A padded cohort UPRN matches once both sides are integers.

docs.title: values-as-published
docs.text:
Decided 2026-10-29. Status: in_force.

Decision. All 107 published columns are kept as text exactly as published, in published order, under the publisher's names, trailing spaces and embedded newlines included. Typed copies are derived beside them and the text is never removed.

Why. The text is the record; the digest over the text proves fidelity. A typed copy is a convenience by a documented rule.
